text:
liz: Heads up — I'm scoping the AWS KMS integration for Redwood Private (VPC) control plane + data-plane. Need alignment on architecture, RBAC mapping, audit logging, envelope encryption, and rotation. Quick Qs below.

pradeep: Nice, this is critical. High-level pattern we've used before: central CMK in security account for control-plane metadata (rotated, audited), and per-customer or per-region CMKs for data-plane objects. But let's list tradeoffs.

alan: TL;DR: use envelope encryption everywhere. Generate a data key with GenerateDataKey, encrypt payload locally, store ciphertext + encrypted data key. KMS calls are then limited to key generation/decrypt during startup or cache refresh.

liz: Agreed on envelope. Specifics: 1) Should control-plane and data-plane keys be separate CMKs? 2) Can we host CMKs in a central security account and grant cross-account access to the private control-plane in customer VPCs? 3) How to map Redwood RBAC -> IAM roles for CMK access?

pradeep: 1) Separate CMKs is simpler and lower blast radius: control-plane CMK for secrets (service tokens, config blobs), data-plane CMKs for customer datasets. 2) Yes, central CMK + grants works well. Use key policy to allow security/admin roles and then use grants or IAM allow for service roles in control-plane account. Avoid relying solely on account root.

alan: 3) Map RBAC to IAM roles: create a service role per control-plane instance group (e.g., redwood-controlplane-role@ACCOUNT). In key policy add a Principal for the IAM role ARN or allow via IAM with kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey. Keep KMS key policy minimal; prefer explicit grants for ephemeral worker nodes to reduce policy churn.

sara: Note on grants: grants are faster (no policy evaluation each call) and better at high QPS. Use GenerateDataKey for writes and a short-lived grant (or re-use a grant) for decrypts if the workload is bursty. But keep careful bookkeeping for grant creation/retire.

marco: For Private on-prem deployments we also need an offline rotation story and possibly HSM integration. If customer chooses AWS KMS in their VPC, central account grants still apply if peering/shared services exist. For air-gapped, we fall back to local HSM or customer-managed KMS and document mapping.

liz: Audit logging: which CloudTrail events to monitor and how to tie to our RBAC/audit logs?

kms-bot: Suggestion: enable CloudTrail Data Events for kms.amazonaws.com and configure a dedicated trail to an audited S3 bucket + Glacier lifecycle. Filter events: GenerateDataKey, Decrypt, Encrypt, CreateGrant, RetireGrant, EnableKeyRotation, CreateKey, UpdateKeyPolicy.

pradeep: Also forward KMS CloudTrail to our SIEM (CloudWatch -> Kinesis Firehose -> Splunk/Datadog). Correlate with our app-level audit: include principal ARN + request ID in service logs so we can tie a KMS Decrypt event to a user action.

alan: Example minimal key policy for cross-account grantability (central CMK):

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Id": "key-policy-central-cmk",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "EnableCrossAccountAccess",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-security-admin"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowUseByControlPlaneRoles",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/redwood-controlplane-role"},
      "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:Encrypt"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

alan: That policy is intentionally permissive in the example; in prod tighten the Principal ARNs and actions. Also avoid embedding user ARNs — prefer roles.

liz: Rotation: are we OK with AWS automatic yearly rotation for symmetric CMKs? Or do we need faster rotation windows for regulatory reasons? And how do we re-encrypt stored envelope-encrypted objects when the CMK rotates?

pradeep: AWS automatic rotation for symmetric CMKs rotates annually; AWS keeps needed prior key material so existing ciphertext still decrypts. If regulator demands N-day rotation, we need custom rotation using re-encryption jobs: generate new data keys and re-encrypt objects. We should provide a migration job (lambda or batch) that reads object, decrypts with old key, re-encrypts with new data key encrypted under new CMK.

sara: Implementation detail: mark metadata with key-id/kms-key-arn and key-version id (if we record it). That allows selective re-encrypt jobs. Don't blindly re-encrypt everything at once; do it by last-accessed or policy.

marco: For customer-controlled KMS (when customers bring their own key), we must support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK). Enforce that customer provides a key policy that grants our control-plane role decrypt/generateDataKey, and we document required CloudTrail + IAM conditions.

liz: What about performance/latency — generating data keys on every request is expensive. Our SDK/runtime has a data-key cache. Any guidance on TTL/size?

alan: Cache data keys in memory keyed by key-id + usage context, TTL ~5-15m depending on risk. For large fleets use local LRU cache + fallback to KMS. Do not persist plaintext data key. Use ephemeral caches per process.

sara: Also consider local envelope key derived from data key for sub-requests (eg HMAC key derived) to reduce KMS calls. Track when cache miss leads to GenerateDataKey and alert if sudden spike (could indicate expiry or attack).

liz: RBAC question: how do we map product-level roles (admin, ops, read-only) to KMS permissions? We don't want product admins to decrypt customer data unless allowed.

pradeep: Keep data-plane CMKs scoped by customer. For admin tasks, create a separate support-temporary-decrypt flow: require approval workflow, create a short-lived grant to a support role with kms:Decrypt and log everything. Automate grant creation with an approval ticket system. Grants can be retired programmatically.

marco: For emergency incident access, we can have an "incident" grant issuer that requires MFA and SSO approval; make it auditable.

liz: Any pitfalls we've seen in previous setups?

alan: Watch out for cross-account KMS limits and grant quotas. Also IAM policy vs key policy precedence confusion — remember key policy is authoritative unless you use a grant. Test using kms:SimulatePrincipalPolicy and CloudTrail to validate.

sara: If using AWS PrivateLink for control-plane to KMS endpoints across VPCs, ensure endpoint policies don't accidentally block cross-account keys. Also ensure AWS KMS VPC endpoints are allowed in the key policy.

infra-bot: Reminder: run the KMS integration checklist in staging: connectivity, regional fallbacks, grant lifecycle, cloudtrail logs present, data key cache behavior, retention and rotation test.

liz: OK. Action items: 1) pradeep to draft central CMK key policy + grant template. 2) alan to write envelope encryption SDK example and data-key cache impl. 3) sara to document audit pipeline and SIEM mapping. 4) marco to draft BYOK customer instructions and incident grant flow.

pradeep: I'll put a PR with key policy templates and a short runbook in the repo by EOD.

alan: I'll attach a sample SDK snippet in the PR showing GenerateDataKey + local encrypt/decrypt pattern.

sara: I'll add CloudTrail filters and SIEM dashboard items to the security playbook.

liz: Thanks all — ping me once PRs are up. :thumbsup:
